name: Humanoid
summary: A humanoid robot (Unitree G1, Unitree H1 or Apptronik Apollo) learns to walk in MuJoCo, thousands at once on a GPU, on a flat floor or round a circuit, and to get up after a fall
help:
A humanoid robot in MuJoCo (models from MuJoCo Menagerie): Robot sets which. Unitree G1 (the default; 1.3 m, 35 kg, 29 joints), Unitree H1 (1.8 m, 51 kg, 19 joints) or Apptronik Apollo (1.7 m, 81 kg, 32 joints). Each robot has its own policies: their file names say which (humanoid_walk_… is the G1's, humanoid_h1_walk_…, humanoid_apollo_standup_…), a run uses only the chosen robot's and leaves the others as they are, so switching robot loses nothing.

Ground: Flat floor, or Circuit: a 38 x 18 m rectangle whose line the robot follows: bumps, a slope to a 0.5 m plateau, blocks, 64 moving tiles, 10 steps up and 10 down, a square of smooth ice (friction 0.08), and a yard of practice stairs.

Learn to walk: a policy (a neural network that, 50 times a second, turns what the robot senses, the speed asked, the beat of its steps and an elevation map of the ground ahead from its head camera into targets for its joints) learns by trial and error (PPO) to walk at the speed asked along its line. 4096 robots on an NVIDIA GPU with MuJoCo Warp, up to 512 on the CPU (to try, not to learn). Pushes, odd starts and sensor noise make it robust. Training: Continue carries on from this robot's policy with the most experience, among those wired in and the checkpoints stopped runs left on this machine, with its optimizer's state; Start over learns from nothing. It ends three minutes before the run's Stop after, so the policy is always written. An episode is replayed in 3D every few seconds (channel robot); numbers go to channel train. Finish now (control channel) stops and keeps the best.

Learn to stand up: each try starts with the robot lying on the flat floor where a fall left it, with 10 s to get up and stay up. At first an upward pull on its torso of 80 % of its weight makes it possible; each time it gets up in more than 60 % of tries the help goes down by 5 %, to none. Several hours on a GPU.

Walk: the robot's newest policy wired in (or Policy file) walks it live round the circuit (esasim.humanoid/1), lap after lap; heading beyond 90° walks it the other way. On the Playground you drive it (the view's drive pad or the keyboard) over sand the feet sink into, 10 cm of water that drags at them, gravel, stepping stones, curbs, ice and steps. From the view's bar: speed, heading, Reset, and Push: a hand that pushes the part of the robot clicked, the way the camera looks (Push strength: as a shove of that many m/s to the whole robot). After a fall, with a stand-up policy of this robot wired in, it gets up on its own (put back on its feet if still down after 10 s); without one, it is set on its feet 3 s later. Events (channel event): what it walks on, falls, laps.

Tuned on the G1; the H1 and the Apollo learn the same task scaled to their size, and may need longer or some tuning.

Packages: torch, mujoco, and for the GPU mujoco-warp and warp-lang.

inputs.label: Policy
inputs.help: Policies (.pt), walking and stand-up, of any robot: each run uses only those of the robot chosen (Walk: the newest of each kind)

outputs.label: Policy
outputs.help: humanoid_[h1_|apollo_]walk_[circuit_]<date>_<NN>.pt or humanoid_[h1_|apollo_]standup_<date>_<NN>.pt: the best policy (network, input scaling, optimizer, robot, ground, score)

outputs.label: Learning curve
outputs.help: training.csv (Learn to walk) or standup.csv (Learn to stand up)

params.label: What to do
params.help: Learn to walk: walking along its line at the speed asked. Learn to stand up: getting up from the floor after a fall (flat floor). Walk: live, with the newest policies

params.label: Robot
params.help: G1: 1.3 m, 35 kg, 29 joints. H1: 1.8 m, 51 kg, 19 joints. Apollo: 1.7 m, 81 kg, 32 joints. Each learns and walks with its own policies only

params.label: Run on
params.help: auto: the NVIDIA GPU when there is one (MuJoCo Warp), else the CPU

params.label: Ground
params.help: Circuit: rough ground, slopes, tiles, ice and stairs round a rectangle. Playground (Walk): sand, water, gravel, stones, curbs, ice and steps, driven by hand

params.label: Robots learning at once
params.help: Learn to walk, Learn to stand up; at most 512 on the CPU

params.label: Minutes
params.help: How long it learns or walks; it stops 3 minutes before the run's Stop after so the policy is kept

params.label: Pushes up to (m/s)
params.help: A shove every 5 to 10 s while it learns; 0: none

params.label: Replay every (s)
params.help: How often an episode is replayed in the 3D view

params.label: Training
params.help: Continue: carry on from this robot's policy with the most experience (wired in, or checkpoints stopped runs left on this machine), with its optimizer; Start over: learn from nothing

params.label: Walking speed (m/s)
params.help: Walk: the speed it starts at (the view's slider changes it)

params.label: Heading (degrees)
params.help: Walk: on the circuit, beyond ±90° it goes round the other way (clockwise); on the flat floor, the way it walks

params.label: Walking policy
params.help: Walk: which of this robot's walking policies wired in to use (empty: the newest)

params.label: After a fall
params.help: Walk: with a stand-up policy wired in, it gets up on its own (put back on its feet if still down after 10 s); else, or with Put back on its feet, it is set on its feet 3 s later
